analysis: Grid-based cavity/concavity search (LIGSITE-style) on DENV NS1 to find conserved concave sites not prioritized by prior flat-patch / wing passes
key_result: NS1 has NO deep buried druggable-style pocket (largest all-directions-enclosed cavity = 6 grid cells). It is a flat, elongated beta-sheet sandwich. Confirms it is intrinsically a hard de novo target.
caveats: Discontinuous in sequence (61-63 / 154 / 180-183 / 198 / 218) - conformational epitope, only valid on folded NS1; will not present on denatured antigen.
Only mildly concave (2.4 A deep) - better than the flat beta-ladder but NOT a deep pocket. A meaningful but modest geometric improvement.
relSASA ~0.20 is exposed but not highly so - some lining residues (e.g. 187-189) bury on assembly; the 8-residue set is the assembly-stable subset.

Region overlaps domain-I/connector, NOT the pre-locked Direction B beta-ladder epitope. Would be a NEW epitope direction ('Direction C'), needs its own DENV1-4 interface verification and Zika/flavivirus cross-reactivity check before adoption.
Concavity computed on a single static DENV structure; not validated against conformational flexibility.
recommendation: Worth a small exploratory RFantibody/binder pilot as a 3rd epitope direction, treated as STRETCH. Does not displace the locked Direction B primary. Verify pan-serotype interface + flavivirus cross-reactivity first.
